description: Curvature (Laplacian of height, 1/m) mapped to −1..1: positive on ridges and convex breaks, negative in valleys and hollows — for rock exposure, soil and sediment masks

scale.description: Curvature (1/m) that maps to ±1; smaller values exaggerate.

radius_px.description:
Stencil half-width in samples (1..=16): 1 reacts to every bump, larger radii read
ridges and valleys at landscape scale.

description: D8 flow accumulation: upstream drainage area per cell (log-scaled 0..1 mask by default) — rivers, wetness, erosion seeding

log_scale.description: Output ln(1 + area) / ln(1 + N) in 0..1 (true) or the raw upstream cell count (false).

method.description: Routing: `d8` (single steepest neighbour), `dinf` (Tarboton facets, smoother streams) or `mfd` (Freeman, most diffuse).

oneOf.description: Single steepest neighbour (O'Callaghan & Mark 1984): fast, 45° quantised.
Tarboton 1997: steepest of eight triangular facets, flow split between its two neighbours.

Freeman 1991 multiple-flow-direction: flow shared among all lower neighbours in proportion
to slope^1.1 — the most diffuse (hillslope wash, wetness); streams come out wide.

description: Slope mask 0..1 (gradient angle / max_deg) — feed into multiply to attenuate by steepness

max_deg.description: Slope that maps to 1.0 in the mask (degrees, (0, 90]).

description: Classify every cell into a biome by ordered rules on height, slope (0..1) and wetness (0..1); outputs the class id map (1-based rule index, 0 = none)

rules.description:
Rules in priority order; class ids are 1-based positions, 0 = unclassified. Empty = a
temperate default set (beach, grassland, forest, rock, snow).

BiomeRule.description:
One biome rule: every given range must hold; a range on an input that is not connected
never matches. Rules are tried in order; the first match wins.

description: Classify the sea floor below `level_m`: 1 sand on the shelf above the wave base, 2 rock on steep slopes, 3 mud in deep still water, 4 reef on a shallow gentle shelf away from river sediment (optional `rivers` and `shore` masks); 0 = land

sand_max_depth_m.description: Wave base: sand is sorted and kept moving down to this depth (metres, > 0).

mud_min_depth_m.description: Below this depth the water is still enough for fine sediment to settle: mud (metres, ≥ wave base).

rock_slope_deg.description: Submarine slopes steeper than this (degrees, (0, 90)) hold no sediment: bare rock.

reef_depth_m.description: Reef band: depths [min, max] where a gentle, sediment-free shelf becomes reef. `[0, 0]` disables reefs.

river_reach_m.description: How far (metres) river mouths keep the shelf sandy rather than reef.

description: Snow cover 0..1 from height alone: a soft snow line, retention that falls with slope, sun-facing slopes melt, windward slopes scour — for biome rules, scatter and colour overlays

snow_line_m.description: Height where cover reaches half, metres.

transition_m.description: Width of the soft transition around the snow line, metres (> 0).

max_slope_deg.description: Slope (degrees, (0, 90]) at which snow no longer holds; retention falls linearly to 0 there.

sun_azimuth_deg.description: Compass direction of the sun (degrees clockwise from north; 180 = south, the northern-hemisphere default).

sun_strength.description: How much sun-facing slopes lose, 0..1 (0 = aspect ignored).

wind_azimuth_deg.description: Compass direction the wind blows from, degrees clockwise from north.

wind_strength.description: How much windward slopes lose to scouring, 0..1 (0 = wind ignored).

description: Wind (aeolian) transport after Werner's slab model: sand hops downwind, stops in wind shadows and on sand, and the angle of repose holds — dunes and ripples; optional `sand` mask (0..1) says what can move

iterations.description: Steps; every step moves up to one slab per sandy cell.

wind_azimuth_deg.description: Compass direction the wind blows from, degrees clockwise from north (270 = westerly).

hop_m.description: Saltation hop length in metres (≥ one cell). Default: 4 cells.

slab_m.description:
Slab thickness in metres (> 0). Default: a quarter of the cell size — thinner slabs never
cast wind shadows and only roughen the surface.

shadow_deg.description: Lee slopes steeper than this, seen along the wind, are wind shadows (Werner: 15°).

deposit_on_sand.description: Probability a hopping slab stops on sand.

deposit_on_bare.description: Probability a hopping slab stops on bare ground (mask < 0.5).

description: Coastal erosion: waves cut the shore within `band_m` above `level_m` by its ocean exposure and lay the material on the adjacent sea floor — cliff retreat, wave-cut platforms, beaches; outputs the terrain and a `shore` mask of wave work

band_m.description: How far above the level the waves reach (notch height / storm run-up), metres (> 0).

rate_m.description: Metres taken off a fully exposed shore cell per step (> 0).

description: Particle (droplet) hydraulic erosion after Beyer: seeded droplets follow the slope with inertia, erode through a brush and deposit as they slow — gullies and fans; outputs the terrain and the signed `delta`

param_schema.title: DropletParams
param_schema.description: Droplet erosion parameters (Beyer's defaults, metres scaled by the sample spacing).

droplets.description:
Number of droplets (1..=5 000 000). Aim for 1–2 per cell: 512² wants ~400 000; fewer gives
diffuse, unstructured lowering, more deepens the same gullies.

max_steps.description: Steps a droplet may travel before it is dropped (8..=256).

inertia.description: Direction inertia 0..1 (0 follows the gradient exactly).

min_capacity.description: Minimum capacity so droplets on flats still carry a little.

deposit.description: Fraction of surplus sediment deposited per step, 0..1.

erode.description: Fraction of the capacity deficit eroded per step, 0..1.

description: Hydraulic erosion (virtual pipes / shallow water): rain flows downhill, dissolves, carries and deposits sediment; outputs terrain, water depth and suspended sediment

dt.description: Time step in seconds ((0, 1]; 0.02 is stable for the pipe model).

rain_rate.description: Rain in metres of water per second.

max_concentration.description: Suspended sediment cap as a fraction of water depth (excess settles the same step).

description: Karst sinkholes (dolines): seeded bowl or collapse depressions on flat, soluble ground — `density_per_km2`, radius and depth ranges, `max_slope_deg`, `min_spacing_m`; optional `soluble` mask (0..1); outputs the carved terrain and a `sinkholes` floor mask

density_per_km2.description: Sinkholes per km² of eligible ground (> 0).

max_slope_deg.description: Steepest ground a sinkhole forms on, degrees (0, 90).

min_spacing_m.description: Closest two centres may be, metres (≥ 0).

oneOf.description: Smooth subsidence bowl: a raised-cosine dip.
Collapse pit: steep rim over the outer 25 % of the radius, flat floor inside.

description: Fluvial (stream-power) erosion: channels incise in proportion to drainage area^m × slope, implicit and unconditionally stable; outputs the eroded terrain and an `incision` depth map; an optional `hardness` field (0..1) drops the erodibility to a tenth on hard rock

k.description:
Erodibility K: metres of incision per step for unit drainage area and unit slope
(`dz = -K·A^m·S`, A in m², S dimensionless). 1e-3 carves visible valleys on a 5 km world
in 20 steps; 1e-4 is subtle, 1e-2 is a badlands.

m.description: Area exponent m (0.3–0.6 in nature; n is fixed at 1 for the implicit solve).

uplift_m.description: Uniform uplift per step in metres (0 = none); outlets rise too, so base level is kept.

method.description: Flow routing used for the drainage area.

oneOf.description: Single steepest neighbour (O'Callaghan & Mark 1984): fast, 45° quantised.
Tarboton 1997: steepest of eight triangular facets, flow split between its two neighbours.

Freeman 1991 multiple-flow-direction: flow shared among all lower neighbours in proportion
to slope^1.1 — the most diffuse (hillslope wash, wetness); streams come out wide.

description: Thermal erosion: material steeper than the talus angle slides downhill (mass-conserving Jacobi steps); an optional `hardness` field (0..1, e.g. from `jd.terrain.strata@1`) lets hard rock hold near-vertical faces and shed at a tenth of the rate

talus_deg.description: Angle of repose in degrees (sand ≈ 30–35, scree ≈ 35–40).

iterations.description: Jacobi steps (1..=1000); more steps move material further.

rate.description: Fraction of the excess that moves per step, (0, 0.25]; 0.25 is the stable maximum.

description: Box blur (tile-local, reads through the halo; radius ≤ world.halo)

radius.description: Box-blur radius in pixels (1..=4; must not exceed the world's tile halo).

description: Terraces: quantise heights into steps of `step_m` with a soft riser — mesas, rice paddies, strata

softness.description: 0 = hard steps, 1 = untouched; in between blends the step edge over that fraction of the riser.

offset_m.description: Shift the step boundaries by this many metres.

description: Priority-flood depression filling: raises pits to their spill level so every cell drains; `lakes` = water depth of the filled basins

epsilon_m.description: Extra rise per step across filled flats so they still drain (metres; 0 = perfectly flat lakes).

description: Carve river channels where flow accumulates (depressions filled first); outputs the carved terrain and a 0..1 river mask

threshold.description: Log-scaled flow accumulation (0..1) above which a cell is a river channel.

depth_m.description: Incision depth at the largest rivers, metres.

method.description: Flow routing used to find channels: `d8`, `dinf` (fewer parallel-line artefacts) or `mfd` (wide, diffuse).

oneOf.description: Single steepest neighbour (O'Callaghan & Mark 1984): fast, 45° quantised.
Tarboton 1997: steepest of eight triangular facets, flow split between its two neighbours.

Freeman 1991 multiple-flow-direction: flow shared among all lower neighbours in proportion
to slope^1.1 — the most diffuse (hillslope wash, wetness); streams come out wide.

description: Ocean mask (1 below `level_m` where connected to the border; inland basins stay dry) with a soft shoreline, and water `depth` in metres

shore_m.description: Shoreline softness: the ocean mask fades from 1 to 0 over this many metres above the level.

visibility_m.description:
Water clarity as the depth (metres) at which the bottom fades out: ~30 for crystal-clear
tropical water, ~15 open ocean, ~3 for a murky estuary. Drives the viewport's Beer–Lambert
absorption per colour channel and the baked water maps; the ocean mask itself ignores it.

tint.description:
Colour of the suspended matter that scatters back out of the water (RGB 0..1): blue-green
plankton, brown silt, green algae. Dominates as the water gets murkier.

wind_speed_mps.description:
Wind speed 10 m above the sea, m/s (0 = calm): 3 ripples, 8 a moderate sea, 20 a gale. Sets
the wave height and length the viewport animates (`ocean.waves`: JONSWAP growth capped at
the fully developed Pierson–Moskowitz sea); the ocean mask ignores it.

fetch_km.description: Fetch, km: how far the wind has blown over open water. Omit for a fully developed sea.

wind_azimuth_deg.description: Where the wind blows FROM, degrees clockwise from north; waves travel the opposite way.

description: Topographic wetness index ln(a / tan β) normalised to 0..1 — wet valley floors high, steep ridges low (biome/moisture masks); `method` picks d8 / dinf / mfd routing

method.description: Flow routing for the drainage area: `d8` (channel-like streaks), `dinf` (smoother) or `mfd` (diffuse moisture).

oneOf.description: Single steepest neighbour (O'Callaghan & Mark 1984): fast, 45° quantised.
Tarboton 1997: steepest of eight triangular facets, flow split between its two neighbours.

Freeman 1991 multiple-flow-direction: flow shared among all lower neighbours in proportion
to slope^1.1 — the most diffuse (hillslope wash, wetness); streams come out wide.

description: Load a heightmap from the project's assets/ (PNG 16-bit, EXR, TIFF, RAW, or a binary FBX mesh rasterised over its footprint) and resample it onto the world grid

param_schema.title: InputParams
param_schema.description: How to interpret a foreign file.

path.description: File inside the project's `assets/` directory (png, exr, tif/tiff, r16, r32).

range_m.description: Height range the full 16-bit span maps to (quantised PNG/TIFF/r16); ignored for float data.

size_px.description: Width and height in pixels — required for headerless RAW files.

north_up.description: Row 0 of the file is north (true, the usual image convention) or south (the field convention).

nodata.description:
Sample value meaning "no data" (filled with the lowest valid height). Default: the GeoTIFF
`GDAL_NODATA` tag when present, otherwise none; non-finite samples are always treated as nodata.

description: 0/1 mask of the cells whose class id equals `id` (feed a `jd.biome.classify@1` map)

id.description: Class id to select (1-based rule position from `jd.biome.classify@1`).

description: a + b
a × b (use a 0..1 mask as b to attenuate)
Linear remap of [from0, from1] to [to0, to1], optional clamp
in × factor
Fractal noise heightfield (OpenSimplex2/Perlin/… × fBm/ridged/ping-pong), parameters in metres

param_schema.title: NoiseParams
param_schema.description: Parameters of a noise heightfield generator.

seed.description: Seed (combined with the world seed by the caller when desired).

feature_size_m.description: Feature size in metres (wavelength of the first octave).

height_range_m.description: Output height range in metres: noise ∈ [-1,1] maps to [min, max].

offset_m.description: Offset of the sampling origin in metres.

oneOf.description: OpenSimplex2 (fast, isotropic). Default.
OpenSimplex2S (smoother).
Improved Perlin.
Value noise.
Cubic value noise.
Cellular / Worley (F1 distance).
Single octave.
Fractal Brownian motion. Default.
Ridged multifractal (mountain ridges).
Ping-pong (terraced/billowy).

description: Sediment infill of the sea floor: sand and mud cells (from a `seabed` class map) rise towards the local mean over `smooth_m`, capped at `max_fill_m` and `level_m`; rock, reef and land are untouched

level_m.description: Sea level, metres: sediment never builds above it.

smooth_m.description: Smoothing reach, metres (> 0): hollows narrower than this fill in.

max_fill_m.description: Thickest sediment layer laid down anywhere, metres (≥ 0).

strength.description: How much of the infill to apply, 0..1 (1 = level the hollow completely).

description: Publishes its input as a named heightfield layer

layer.description: Layer name the result is published under.

description: Brush strokes (raise/lower with smooth falloff) recorded as data: non-destructive, replayable, undo removes a whole stroke

strokes.description: Recorded brush strokes, applied in order on top of the input.

points.description: Polyline in layer metres: `[u east, v north]` from the south-west corner (row 0 = south).

strength_m.description: Height added at the centre for `raise` (negative lowers), metres.

StrokeMode.description: What a stroke does to the heights under the brush.

oneOf.description: Add `strength_m` (negative digs).
Blend towards the local mean (box filter ~ radius/4) by `amount`.
Blend towards the height under the first point by `amount`.

description: Layered rock hardness (0..1): repeating hard-cap / soft-bed cycles of `layer_m`, tilted by `dip_deg` towards `dip_azimuth_deg`, bed surfaces undulating by `warp_m` — feed it to the `hardness` input of thermal and stream-power erosion for mesas, buttes and stepped canyon walls; re-evaluate after the surface moves

layer_m.description: Thickness of one hard+soft cycle, metres (> 0).

hard_fraction.description: Share of each cycle that is hard caprock, 0..1 (the rest is soft).

hard.description: Hardness of the cap, 0..1 (1 = holds vertical cliffs, erodes at a tenth of the rate).

transition.description: Width of the hard↔soft transition as a fraction of the cycle, 0..0.5.

dip_deg.description: Dip of the beds, degrees from horizontal, [0, 60].

dip_azimuth_deg.description: Direction the beds dip towards, degrees clockwise from north.

warp_m.description: Undulation of the bed surfaces, metres (≥ 0): 0 for flat beds.
